sentences.text: Allosaurus was a large theropod characterized by a massive skull, short neck, long tail, and reduced forelimbs.
Its light skull contained dozens of sharp, serrated teeth that were modestly proportioned for its size.
Skin impressions reveal scales up to two centimeters wide on the tail and neck of juvenile specimens.
The genus Allosaurus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877, describing the first definitive fossil remains.
This discovery occurred during the Bone Wars, a rivalry between Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope that spurred fossil discoveries in the Western US.
Antrodemus was the accepted name for over 50 years until James H. Madsen argued that Allosaurus should be used due to the poor quality of Antrodemus's diagnostic material.
The International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature ratified a petition in December 2023 to designate specimen USNM 4734 as the neotype for Allosaurus fragilis.
As the most abundant large predator in the Morrison Formation, Allosaurus was an apex predator likely hunting ornithopods, stegosaurids, and sauropods.
Robert T. Bakker compared Allosaurus to Cenozoic saber-toothed mammals, noting adaptations like reduced jaw muscles, increased neck muscles, and the ability to open jaws extremely wide.

Research deems the hatchet jaw attack unlikely, reinterpreting the wide gape as an adaptation for delivering muscle-driven bites to large prey, with weaker jaw muscles being a trade-off for the widened gape.
Histological analysis suggests Allosaurus stopped growing at around 22 to 28 years of age, similar to other large theropods like Tyrannosaurus.
Evidence for cannibalism in Allosaurus includes shed teeth found among rib fragments and tooth marks on shoulder blades.

In 1972, Kristen Petersen and colleagues documented pathologies in Cleveland-Lloyd Quarry specimens, including rib fractures, joint stiffness, fused tail vertebrae, and possible bite-induced bone amputations.
The specimen known as Big Al preserves 19 distinct pathologies across its skeleton.
These hollow spaces are interpreted as being occupied by air sacs used for respiration, a feature also found in modern birds.
The high number of Allosaurus found at single sites suggests they may have lived in groups.
Madsen suggested that unfused pubic bones in Allosaurus might indicate sexual dimorphism to facilitate egg-laying, but this proposal has not gained further support.
Allosaurus is classified within the family Allosauridae.
Allosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian ages of the Late Jurassic period.
Allosaurus lived during the late Jurassic period, between 155 and 145 million years ago.
Allosaurus lived from the Oxfordian to the Berriasian stages, between 161.5 and 137.05 million years ago.
Statistical analyses between 1996 and 1999 suggested that variations in Allosaurus fossils from the Morrison Formation represent individual differences rather than distinct species.
The validity of the European species Allosaurus europaeus has been debated, with some studies suggesting it is a synonym of A. fragilis, a doubtful name, or requires re-evaluation.
